title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks

primary_sources.paraphrase: Full text, v2. Zero-shot Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS against AutoGluon baselines trained on 2023, on hourly heat load of two German district heating networks (Munich private, Flensburg public). 2024, a 24-hour forecast every day (366 starts), 12-week context, realized future temperature. Adds a forecast-weather sensitivity run (208 starts) and a 52-week week-ahead appendix. 95% bootstrap intervals.

Abstract page: submitted 20 Aug 2026, revised 6 Oct 2026. Headline: both zero-shot models beat all trained baselines on deterministic accuracy in the full-year benchmarks; Chronos-2 is best (CVRMSE 12.48% on the main data set), TabPFN-TS close (13.07%). The main benchmark assumes perfect weather.

Authors' repository, MIT code, archived on Zenodo. Ships the Flensburg heat and temperature data with scripts for the 2024 full-year runs of TabPFN-TS, Chronos-2 and AutoGluon and for a Flensburg forecast-weather run with IFS temperature (leads 11 to 34 h). Munich inputs are excluded. Names the journal version (Energy and AI).
Hub record of the central model: licence apache-2.0, created 2025-10-30, head 29ec376 (2026-06-05), about 119.5M parameters, not gated.

Commit history of the weights repository: weights and config were added on 30 Oct 2025 (commit 95a9710); later commits, up to 29ec376 on 5 Jun 2026, are README, tag or deployment-guide edits by their titles.

relevance.rationale: Hourly district heat load, not electric load, so target_match is 2. The benchmark and every comparison with trained baselines are day-ahead (24 hourly steps); a week-ahead appendix (168 steps, 52 forecasts) compares only the two zero-shot models, so horizon_match stays 2. Ambient temperature is the sole weather input and is supplied as a known-future covariate, measured in the main benchmark and as archived forecasts in a sensitivity run: the same two regimes as ours, and the same central model as our primary comparison.

checks.notes: pre_registered: neither the full text nor the repository mentions a plan or registration. training_overlap_risk is about our run: the Chronos-2 weights file was committed on 2025-10-30 (Hugging Face commit list), before our first scored week (2025-11-10), so all 52 weeks follow it. independent_replication: one research call and one search found none; the Flensburg run is the authors' own external validation. evidence_strength is moderate: public code and a public data set (Flensburg) make part of the result reproducible and the test window is a full year, but there is no pre-registration or replication, the main (Munich) data is private, and the baselines did not all get the same inputs: only the tabular models, DeepAR and TFT use future temperature, and the baselines see history from 2023 rather than the 12-week window, hence 'partly'. The paper's intervals are 95%, not 90%, so ci90 is left out and the intervals are in the claim text. Forecast weather was tested on the two zero-shot models only, on 208 days, so the paper has no forecast-regime comparison against a trained baseline; its IFS data are hindcasts from a later model cycle, which the authors say do not show what was published in 2024. A third-party review of v1 (pith.science, search snippet only) notes that the configuration was chosen on 2024 weeks that are also inside the evaluation year. Central model: Chronos-2 (best scores in the headline); TabPFN-TS is the second model. Licence Apache-2.0 is the Hub record's tag for the Chronos-2 weights. Not verified: the unfiltered Munich baseline values (the research answer gives TFT 14.61%, Direct LGBM 15.87%, AutoGluon ensemble 16.54%, but the fetched table lost that column; the anomaly-excluded table was read directly); the Flensburg CVRMSE values; which network the week-ahead appendix uses; the Chronos-2 revision the authors loaded (only chronos-forecasting 2.2.2 is stated); the TabPFN-TS checkpoint and its licence (the research answer says a non-commercial licence for the TabPFN-3 weights, source not fetched); the journal version in Energy and AI (named by the repository, not fetched). The research answer's statement that the main benchmark covered only 208 starts is wrong: the paper and repository give 366 starts for it and 208 for the sensitivity run.

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: Relevant and sourced: a full-year study with public code in which zero-shot Chronos-2 with temperature as a known-future covariate beats trained baselines on an hourly energy load, under both measured and forecast temperature. Its headline comparison can be re-measured now with amazon/chronos-2 through our adapter against the temperature-only regression, at 168 hours instead of 24 and on electric instead of heat load.
implementation_hint: Central model amazon/chronos-2 (direct_adapter, models/chronos2.py, weights repository amazon/chronos-2, head 29ec376; weights file from 95a9710). Runnable today: zero-shot Chronos-2 with temperature against the temperature-only regression, oracle and forecast regimes, which is the protocol's primary comparison; LightGBM is our nearest match to the paper's tabular baselines. The paper used a 12-week (2,016 h) rolling context and a 24-hour horizon; ours is 168 hours, which the paper covers only in an appendix without trained baselines. Second model TabPFN-TS: a FoundationForecast wrapper exists (ff_univariate, models_ff/run_ff.py), so it would run without temperature, unlike in the paper; its weights licence is reported as non-commercial (not verified). The paper's own baselines are AutoGluon TimeSeries 1.5.0 models, which we do not run.

receipt.claimed: Zero-shot Chronos-2 with temperature as a known-future covariate has the lowest error on hourly district heat load, ahead of every trained baseline: day-ahead CVRMSE 12.48% over 2024 in Munich with measured temperature (11.83% against 14.24% for TFT, the best trained model, after excluding 24 flagged days). With archived forecast temperature its error rises to 12.56% from 11.41% over 208 days.
receipt.horizon_mismatch: The paper forecasts district heat load in two German networks 24 hours ahead; we forecast PJM electric load (JC, DOM) 168 hours ahead. Its trained baselines are AutoGluon models fitted on 2023 (best: TFT) that did not all receive future temperature; ours is the temperature-only regression given the identical temperature series. Its headline uses measured temperature, and forecast temperature was tested only on the zero-shot models with later-cycle IFS hindcasts; our primary comparison is in the forecast regime with lead-matched archived forecasts. Its week-ahead appendix has no trained baseline. Metric is CVRMSE there, the protocol's error ratio here.
